document.abstract: The Spectrum Compatible HDTV (SC-HDTV) system achieves the encoding of a 28.9 MHz source signal for transmission over a conventional 6 MHz channel. The new signal format reduces mutual interference between existing NTSC broadcasts and the new high-definition broadcasts to such a degree that significant amounts of currently “taboo”-ed spectrum space become available. As a result, every existing NTSC station can be assigned a second 6 MHz high definition channel. The HD encoding drastically reduces the required transmitter power which reduces the interference into NTSC broadcasts while at the same time providing immunity against interference by NTSC signals.

authors.bio: Wayne Bretl is a staff consulting engineer in Electronic Systems R&D at Zenith Electronics Corporation. He has worked there and at Motorola in color TV and new-product areas. He holds several patents on various signal processing techniques and is a member of IEEE, SMPTE, and AES. He serves on the Advanced Television Systems Committee Technical Groups on High Definition, Enhanced 525-line, and Improved NTSC Television.
authors.name: Wayne Bretl

authors.bio: Richard Citta obtained his BSEE degree in 1969 from the Illinois Institute of Technology and his MSEE degree in 1971 from the University of Washington. He is presently a manager in the Electronic Systems Research and Development Department of Zenith Electronics Corporation. His group is currently concentrating on developing high-definition television encoding and transmission systems and has been responsible for the advanced development for Zenith's cable TV product division. Mr. Citta has published several technical papers on television and cable systems. He holds 17 U.S. patents with 6 patents pending. In 1988 he was the recipient of the Dr. Adler Award, Zenith's highest award for technical achievement.
authors.name: Richard Citta

authors.bio: Ronald B. Lee was born in 1954 in Chicago, Illinois. He received his BS degree in electrical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1975 and his MS degree in electrical engineering from the University of Illinois, Urbana, in 1976. After graduating he joined Zenith Electronics Corporation, where he has been involved in audio and video signal processing. He is currently a senior project engineer in the Electronic Systems Research and Development Group at Zenith.
authors.name: Ronald Lee

authors.bio: Pieter Fockens is a staff consultant in the Electronic Systems R&D Department of Zenith Electronics Corporation. His special interest is in system studies. Lately he has worked on HDTV systems analysis. Earlier he was involved with television multichannel sound and quadraphonic FM as a member of EIA working groups and with videodisc signal processing and Phonevision, Zenith's early over-the-air pay-TV system. He is an EE Delft (Netherlands) graduate. He co-authored several papers, is holder or co-holder of several patents, and is a member of IEEE.
authors.name: Pieter Fockens
